question: When counselling a family for organ donation after brain-stem death, the news of death and the request for donation should always be communicated in the same conversation to save time.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. The single most important principle in donation counselling is decoupling — separating the notification of death from the request for donation. The family needs time to accept the death before any discussion of donation can be ethically or practically productive.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. The cardinal rule of donation counselling is DECOUPLING: the family must fully absorb the news of death before any donation request is made. Combining both in one conversation causes distress and dramatically reduces consent rates.
